claims.text: The initially solid FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are compositionally homogeneous.
The initially solid FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are fully crystalline and lack segregation-driven surface disorder.
Cu is an inherently lower-melting constituent of the FeNiCrCoCu system.
Elevated temperature preferentially drives Cu from the nanoparticle interior to its surface.
Preferential Cu migration produces a Cu-enriched surface layer.
A Cu-enriched surface layer reduces surface cohesion.
Reduced cohesion at the Cu-enriched surface produces an amorphous or highly disordered interfacial region before complete melting.
Cu enrichment locally lowers the melting temperature and initiates surface premelting.
As temperature rises, the disordered Cu-rich surface layer facilitates inward propagation of melting.
Surface segregation of Cu governs both the onset and progression of melting in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Particles permitting active surface segregation will develop surface disorder before bulk melting and at a lower temperature than the bulk melting temperature.
Thermal pre-homogenization will delay or suppress surface segregation.
Pre-homogenized particles will melt more uniformly and with an onset closer to the bulk melting temperature than particles permitting natural segregation.
The proposed mechanism applies when particles are sufficiently small for surface effects to dominate.
Larger particle size may cause deviations from the proposed Cu-driven surface-premelting behavior.
Oxidizing or other non-vacuum environments may cause deviations by introducing extrinsic effects.
Prior nanoparticle studies in related alloys have indicated that surface phenomena are important.
